text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Around 200 million pounds ($390 million) switches hands in the underworld in prostitution, drugs, gambling and protection rackets, a deputy tells parliament.
- The government puts a stop to public comments on what it will and what it will not do at the forthcoming direct talks on the Cyprus problem.

- The government is pre-empting a meeting by the National Council, an advisory body on the Cyprus problem, by making statements on what the positions of the Greek Cypriot side will be during the direct talks.
- A survey carried out by the communist Akel party gives lawyer and possible candidate in next year's presidential elections Marios Eliades 49 percent support.
- Washington and London are processing elements of a "preliminary agreement" on the Cyprus issue which will be submitted during the direct talks.
- Parliament is expected to approve legislation today which regulates the work of commercial banks and the supervision exercised by the Central Bank.

- The Turkish side appears willing to negotiate on the territorial aspect of the Cyprus dispute, with around 32 percent of Cyprus remaining under Turkish administration in the event of a federal solution. Thirty four percent is occupied today. ($=0.511 pound)
